notes: 11 available - a bare-bones bench night. OUT: John Flinn #19, Kyle Doherty, Matt Watson, Sang Lee (and Andrew Amann, Luke McArdle no-show on the RSVP). With Watson, Flinn, Sang and Kyle all gone, our infield and left-side outfield depth evaporated, so the position math writes most of the lineup for us: SEVEN players go wire-to-wire. Marks is the only shortstop (all 7 at SS). Knight and DiLibero are the ONLY two left fielders left on the roster, so they split LF/LCF for all 7 (Knight LF, DiLibero LCF). And the only pitcher-plus-corner-infield pool we have left - Klatt, Joe McLean, Ed Fitzpatrick, Jon Sorenson - exactly fills P + 1B + 2B + 3B every inning, so none of them can sit either. Klatt pitches innings 1-4 then takes 3B (5-7); Joe plays 2B innings 1-4 then pitches (5-7); Ed is the everyday 3B with Watson out (3B 1-4, 2B 5-7); Sorenson anchors 1B all 7. That leaves four right-siders - Coulombe, Konen, Bruno, Cheever - to rotate C/RCF/RF and soak up every rest. The catcher's mask rotates through Bruno, Cheever, Coulombe and Konen (nobody catches more than twice), and Ryan gets outfield innings too.
sits_note: Eleven bodies, ten gloves - so exactly one lucky soul gets a bench cameo each inning, seven sits total. Tonight the roster is so thin the position chart does the benching for us: seven iron men never touch the pine. Marks (the only shortstop in existence - if he sits, SS becomes folklore), Knight and DiLibero (the last two left fielders standing - they ARE the left side of the outfield), and the entire infield-and-mound crew Klatt, Joe McLean, Ed Fitzpatrick and Sorenson (four humans for the four spots of P/1B/2B/3B - the arithmetic literally cannot spare one). That funnels all seven rests onto the right-side committee: Coulombe, Bruno and Cheever sit twice apiece and Konen - the best glove of the bunch (fewest 2025 errors) - sits just once. Nobody sits back-to-back, nobody sits three times, and everyone bats all game regardless - SIT means a fielding breather, not a benching. Cheever opens and closes on the bench (strongest available gloves out for innings 1 and 7), and the mask passes politely between Bruno, Cheever, Coulombe and Konen so no one's knees file a grievance. Thin night, clean solution.

opponent_lineup.source: 2025 scouting (~38 PA on file, small sample): a pull/left-heavy, right-handed attack - 47% of balls in play go to the LEFT, 25% center, 28% right, with a roughly even infield/outfield split (53/47). Shade the defense LEFT / left-center (Stack Left) and make them beat you the other way.

rules: VALIDATION: every inning fields exactly ten distinct players across P, C, 1B, 2B, 3B, SS, LF, LCF, RCF, RF - one glove per spot, no gaps, nobody cloned. All seven innings check out.
Thin roster (11 available) forces 7 iron men (0 sits): Marks (only SS), Knight + DiLibero (only two LF/LCF), Klatt + Joe McLean + Ed Fitzpatrick + Sorenson (the only P/1B/2B/3B pool).
Pitching split 4/3: Eric Klatt pitches innings 1-4, Joe McLean pitches innings 5-7. Klatt shifts to 3B (5-7); Joe plays 2B (1-4).
Watson out: Ed Fitzpatrick is the everyday 3B (3B innings 1-4, then 2B innings 5-7 when Klatt takes the corner) - plays all 7. Jon Sorenson anchors 1B all 7.
Knight (LF) and DiLibero (LCF) play all 7 - they are the only two left-side outfielders available with Amann and Flinn out.
Catcher rotates among Bruno, Cheever, Coulombe and Konen - nobody catches more than twice; Coulombe also plays right-side OF.
Sits fall on the four right-siders: Coulombe, Bruno, Cheever sit twice; Konen (best glove) sits once. No back-to-back sits.
Batting order = 2026 stats, role-based: Klatt & Joe McLean set the table (top OBP/contact), the run producers cluster 3-4-5 (DiLibero, Marks, Konen), remaining bats by OPS.
